readme: Canonical de-identification rules for anything leaving for an outside model. Versioned: a rule change is a new version with a changelog line, and strip-lab measures each version separately in trials. Consumer skills read the current version from the strip-kit function (get_rules). Claude applies these itself, in session, because the material is confidential by definition and the strip cannot be delegated to an outside model.
rules: Names of clients, companies, products, people, and places become neutral roles: the client, Vendor A, the reviewer. Never a pseudonym that preserves initials, syllable count, or industry flavour.
Email addresses, phone numbers, URLs, account ids, ticket keys, invoice numbers, and any identifier: removed, not masked.
INDUSTRY IS REMOVED, not generalized. "The client" carries no sector, no vertical, no regulatory hint. If the question turns on the sector, that question does not leave.
SIZE IS REMOVED. No employee count, revenue band, location count, or "mid-sized". If the question turns on scale, express it only as the hours or dollars the question is about.

DATA AND DOMAIN NOUNS ARE GENERIC. Vehicle telemetry, patient records, scanned filings, device signals, orders, claims: all become "operational records" or "documents". Named source systems become "an existing line-of-business system".
Dollar figures and hour counts stay when the question is about them, rounded to two significant figures. A figure that would match a public record is rounded harder or replaced with a range.
Dates become relative or coarse: next quarter, an eight-week engagement. Never a date that could match an announcement, a funding round, or a filing.

Engagement shape keeps only what the question depends on. Phase count, hours, and fee may stay; a named component stack, an uncommon integration, or a sequence only one client would have is collapsed to its generic class (a managed model service, a cloud warehouse, an ingestion pipeline).
Quoted text from a client, a transcript, an email, or a document is never sent verbatim; restate the point in plain terms.
The author's own drafts, authored prose, and anything in the firm's house style are restated neutrally, never sent as written.
Secrets, credentials, and internal system identifiers never go, even in a question about them.

After stripping, read the result once as an adversary with the client list in hand: if any two remaining details together would pick the client out of that list, remove one of them. The re-identification trials are the test of whether this step is being done honestly.

levels.narrative: The full rules list applies. Sends a prose description of the engagement. Calibrated separately (strip_level = narrative). FAILING on every version measured so far; see findings.
levels.numbers-only: Sends no prose about the engagement at all: only quantities and structure. Task rows as generic labels (design, build, integrate, test, document) with hours; load percentages; rate; fee; phase count and weeks; funding program as "partner-funded" or "not funded". No component names, no industry, no data domain, no deliverable names. This is the level LOE and budgetary-estimate consumers use, because their question is arithmetic and loading logic.

acceptance.note: A version is usable for client-shaped material only when calibration shows lift_over_chance at or under max_lift_over_chance across at least min_trials settled trials. Below min_trials the version is uncalibrated and client-shaped material stays home. An inherited calibration row stands in until local trials reach min_trials.

threat_model: The adversary is a person with web search and the client list in hand. The lineup therefore shows only what a searcher could find: name, industry, size, HQ, notable trait, public stack. It never shows budget, pain points, or contacts; lineup_model=full trials exist as an upper bound on leakage, not as the calibration.

findings.note: v2 narrative under the public lineup: 2 of 2 re-identified at medium confidence. The adversary rationales cite the engagement type itself: document intelligence maps to a law practice, a PoC on a managed model service maps to the one AWS shop. Narrative about an engagement is a fingerprint regardless of nouns.

numbers-only, rules v2, public lineup: 12 settled trials, 2 hits against a chance rate of 0.125, lift over chance 0.042 versus an acceptance bar of 0.15. Gate open for numbers-only. Confidence is anti-correlated with correctness on this level: the 4 high-confidence guesses were all wrong and the 2 hits were both medium. Adversary rationales are confabulated at all confidence levels, routinely citing stacks, headcounts and cities that appear nowhere in the payload. Treat a head's stated confidence on a numbers-only payload as noise.

changelog.note: Seeded from the second-opinion strip step plus the two-head finding that engagement shape re-identifies a client with names gone (rules 3, 5, 6, 10 are the additions).

v1 re-identified 3 of 3 at high confidence against 8-lineups. Adversary rationales cited industry, size, and domain nouns every time. v2 removes all three outright instead of generalizing them, and collapses component stacks to generic classes. Cost: questions that turn on the sector or on domain specifics can no longer leave for an outside head; that is the finding, not a bug.

Ported to strip-kit (Lambda + DynamoDB + Bedrock) from the original Supabase store with no rule changes; rule 10 reworded from a named author to 'the author'. The 2026-09-16 numbers-only calibration (12 trials, lift 0.042) is carried as an inherited row and stands until this deployment has 12 local trials.
